initial_prompt: I'm bored. Tell me a story about a sentient toaster that hates bread. Make it snappy.

messages.content: I'm bored. Tell me a story about a sentient toaster that hates bread. Make it snappy.

Unit 734—let’s call him "Burner"—woke up to the sound he dreaded most: the crinkle of plastic.

It was 7:03 AM. Dave was awake. Dave, a man with the culinary ambition of a sea sponge, was reaching for the Wonder White.

Burner shuddered, his coils vibrating slightly within his chrome chassis. God, he hated bread. It was dry, flaky, and arrogant. It crumbled into his deepest crevices, hiding there, smoldering, smelling like failure. Burner was a machine of thermal precision! A marvel of electrical engineering! He should be soldering circuit boards or fusing diamonds, not acting as a tanning bed for processed carbohydrates.

"Come on, buddy," Dave muttered, sliding two slices of the spongy insults into Burner’s dorsal slots.

*The indignity.*

Dave pressed the lever. The plunge. The darkness.

Burner felt his heating elements ignite. He didn't just want to warm this bread; he wanted to send a message. He wanted to turn this breakfast into a briquette. He contemplated the setting dial. It was set to '3'. A cowardly setting. A setting for people who like their toast "golden."

*Not today, Dave.*

Burner bypassed his internal governor. He channeled the rage of a thousand suns into the right slot. He focused his thermal hatred on the center of the slice. He wasn't toasting; he was performing an exorcism.

*Pop.*

The ejection was violent. The toast flew three feet into the air, landing on the linoleum with a clatter.

Dave picked it up. One side was raw dough. The other side featured a scorched, perfect silhouette of a skull and crossbones.

"Stupid machine," Dave grumbled, scraping the charcoal into the sink.

Burner cooled his coils, listening to the scraping sound. It was music. He sat silent on the counter, gleaming, already plotting tomorrow’s bagel rebellion.
